articles.title: IIT Roorkee student death: 70 exams postponed, to be held on November 22
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Following the death of a 20-year-old student, allegedly by suicide, at IIT Roorkee , the institute has postponed 70 examinations to November 22, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
The exams were originally scheduled to be held on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The deceased, Ayush Rajauria, was a second-year student of the institute’s BS-MS programme in Mathematics and Computing and hailed from Raj Nagar Extension in Ghaziabad.

According to police, the incident came to light around midnight on Thursday after Kuldeep Singh Negi, a security officer at IIT Roorkee, informed the Kotwali Roorkee police that a student was found dead in room number BS 10 on the second floor of Govind Bhawan hostel.
A purported note left by the deceased was found in his room, in which he allegedly wrote about suffering from depression and being distressed about his life, according to officials.
Officials said Rajauria had been receiving counselling on campus for the past year to cope with mental stress.

Speaking to PTI , Sonika Srivastava, in-charge of the IIT Roorkee's media cell, said the student was being counselled at the campus wellness centre — a facility dedicated to supporting students who may be experiencing depression or other psychological challenges.
She also said that all the students and their families have been informed about the postponement of the exams and the revised scheduled date, November 22.
Police said on Friday (November 13, 2026) that the student's family had been informed and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death was underway.
In a statement, IIT Roorkee has expressed grief over the student's death and extended condolences to his family.

The death has sent shockwaves through students and parents, bringing the focus back on the mental health of IIT students across the country and the rising number of student suicides on campuses of the prestigious institutes.

articles.title: Three phase gram panchayat polls in Bapatla district from November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Elections to 351 gram panchayats in Bapatla district will be conducted in three phases, with the first phase scheduled for November 26, District Collector V. Vinod Kumar announced on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
Addressing a media conference, he said elections would be held for 3,362 wards through 3,770 polling stations. The district has 8,67,954 voters, including 4,23,910 men, 4,43,995 women and 49 others.

The first phase will cover six mandals in the Parchur constituency, while the second will cover seven mandals in the Vemuru and Chirala constituencies. The third phase will cover seven mandals in the Bapatla and Repalle constituencies.

For the first phase, nominations will be accepted from November 15 to 17, followed by scrutiny on November 18. Appeals against rejected nominations can be filed on November 19 and will be resolved the next day. Candidates can withdraw nominations on November 21, when the final list will be published. Polling and counting will take place on November 26, followed by the election of deputy sarpanches.
Under G.O. No. 11, unanimous gram panchayat elections will attract development incentives of ₹15 lakh, ₹25 lakh and ₹50 lakh, depending on population.
The Collector also announced Bapatla municipality elections on November 26. He urged voters to verify their names in the electoral rolls and exercise their franchise.

articles.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Women must get adequate representation in Parliament, legislatures: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 14, 2026) stressed the need for adequate representation of women in Parliament and State legislatures, expressing hope that the Women’s Reservation Bill would be implemented soon. Incidentally, Karnataka is yet to have a woman representative in its Cabinet.

“The Women’s Reservation Bill has been passed in the Rajya Sabha and is yet to be approved by the Lok Sabha. I am hopeful that it will become a reality in the coming Parliament session. Women must get adequate representation in Parliament and State legislatures,” he said.
He was speaking after unveiling the logo of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region conference, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru on November 17 and 18.

Recalling former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s contribution to women’s political empowerment, Mr. Shivakumar said it was his government that had brought in legislation providing 50% reservation for women in local bodies, from panchayats to district-level administration. He said he believed that all political parties supported women’s reservation.

Highlighting women’s presence in important constitutional and administrative positions in Karnataka, he said the Governor, Chief Secretary, Karnataka Legislative Assembly Secretary, Legislative Council Secretary and Deputy Chairperson of the Legislative Council were all women.
“It is a matter of satisfaction that women are holding key positions in the State’s administration. Women are the eyes of a family. When women are empowered, men too become empowered,” he said.

Describing the CWP conference as a historic milestone for Karnataka, Mr. Shivakumar said the State government would extend all support to the first independent CWP India Region conference being held in Bengaluru.

The conference, being organised under the leadership of CWP India Region president D. Purandeswari, is expected to bring together more than 150 women parliamentarians, legislators and presiding officers from India and abroad.
The participants are expected to deliberate on the country’s development and protection of women’s rights, he said.

The government would extend all necessary assistance through Legislative Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed to ensure the successful conduct of the conference, he said.

Mr. Shivakumar also recalled the contributions of former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sucheta Kripalani, the country’s first woman Chief Minister, and President Droupadi Murmu.
Their achievements demonstrated that women could accomplish anything they set their minds to, he added.

articles.title: Four earthquakes recorded in J-K, Ladakh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four earthquakes with magnitudes ranging from 2.9 to 3.9 were recorded across Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh within a span of 11 hours on Saturday (November 14, 2026), the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said.
Of the four tremors, three were recorded in the Chenab Valley region of Jammu and Kashmir, while one struck Leh in the Union Territory of Ladakh, according to NCS updates shared on X .
There were no reports of damage from the earthquake hit areas, police said.
An earthquake of 3.3 magnitude struck Kishtwar district at 2:38 a.m., with the epicentre located at a depth of 15 km.
Another tremor of 3.8 magnitude hit Doda district at 8:48 a.m. The epicentre was identified at a depth of 5 km.
Another 2.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Doda at 1:09 p.m., at a depth of 10 km.
A 3.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Leh, Ladakh, at 10:29 a.m., at a depth of 10 km.

articles.title: Cyclone may bring isolated heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has given a heavy rain forecast for the coastal A.P. from November 18 to 20, though no such warnings have been given on November 16 and 17, when the cyclonic storm is likely to make a landfall.

According to the IMD’s afternoon bulletin, heavy rain is likely at one or two places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and gusty winds, with speed reaching 40-50 kmph, on November 18, 19 and 20. The State may not see much rain during the landfall.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the low-pressure over southeast Bay of Bengal strengthened into a well-marked low pressure. It is very likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression over the same region by Sunday (November 15, 2026). Thereafter, it is likely to move north-northwestwards and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal around November 16.

Weather experts at the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority and IMD have said clarity on the probable landfall location may emerge after depression is formed. At present, weather models are showing varied results, they said.

However, the IMD has said that squally weather, with wind speeds gusting up to 60 kmph, is very likely to prevail near the Southeast Bay of Bengal on November 14 and 15. It may increase further to 70 kmph on November 16 and 17. Near the Southwest Bay of Bengal, the wind speed may touch 80 kmph on November 17, and near the central parts, the gales may touch 75-85 kmph speed from November 17.
The sea condition is likely to be rough to very rough over southeast, southwest and central parts of the Bay from November 15.
Fishermen have been advised to return to coasts by November 15.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

fullParagraphs: Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.

articles.title: No Indians onboard in carrier involved in Mississippi mishap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The bitumen carrier, Atlantic Asphalt, that rammed into riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans does not have Indian crew onboard.

The tanker that apparently lost its steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat with about 180 people aboard on Friday (November 13, 2026). All aboard survived after the crash prompted a massive rescue operation for passengers and crew who plunged into the Mississippi River.
As per government records, on Atlantic Asphalt that can carry some 17,500 tonnes of bitumen used in laying roads, there were no Indians onboard, sources said.
The ship registered in Marshall Islands and owned by a company formally registered in Liberia is manned by a Singapore ship management company which does employ Indian seafarers on its ships.
It is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation, a sprawling Chinese state-owned conglomerate, according to the website MarineTraffic.

The Chinese company overseeing the asphalt tanker in 2022 accounted for nearly a quarter of the global commercial shipbuilding market, according to a report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. It was also the largest military shipbuilder in the world at the time.

Onsite videos show that the ship seemed to have lost control of its steering, if not power, that led to the accident. The boat took in water, tilted and sank along the jetty. Passengers who were thrown into the water were seen wearing lifejackets that would have helped save lives.

In March 2024, container ship Dali, with mostly Indian crew, rammed into a bridge in Baltimore that led to loss of six lives and property damaged leading to the largest marine insurance settlements running to billions of dollars. Dali lost power as well as steering leading to the accident.
Ever Given that blocked Suez Canal traffic for nearly six days in 2021 had 25 Indian crew onboard.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.
Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.
The Redmond, Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.
It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

articles.title: Riots in France: How anti-Government protests spiralled out of control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Smashed windows and ransacked shops. Bloodied teenage protesters. A city hall on fire.
Such scenes shocked France as rioting erupted last month during nationwide protests over high living costs and strained public services.

Government officials have repeatedly blamed far-left radicals and “opportunistic delinquents,” who they say took advantage of mostly peaceful demonstrations ​to attack symbols of State authority and capitalism across France.

But the authorities’ heavy-handed response, including thousands of arrests, police beatings and curbs on marches, has added to the volatile mix of grievances fuelling an anti-Government groundswell that shows no sign of abating before next year’s presidential election, Reuters found.

Reuters journalists reviewed dozens of videos of the violence, attended ‌the court hearings of 26 people accused of taking part and interviewed over 50 Government officials, police officers, attorneys, protesters and witnesses to understand how a movement that began in September with small protests over conditions in State schools spiralled ​into some of the worst civil unrest in years.

Police tactics have faced scrutiny since the start due to the life-changing injuries suffered by some young people, including blown-off hands and lost eyes. United Nations and other human rights experts have also raised concerns about ⁠the arrest of nearly 7,000 minors during sometimes-violent school blockades, which they said was disproportionate.

Images of riot police baton-charging teenagers fanned support for the students from a diverse array of protesters, including parents, teachers, left-wing politicians and trade unionists, who joined their marches.

“We have rights,” said Emilie Berthier de Grandry, 42, who has attended four demonstrations in Paris with her 15-year-old son, Aaron, dressed in an inflatable shark costume. “We’re not going to let ourselves be pushed around.”

Nationwide demonstrations on October 17 also brought a resurgence of so-called yellow-vest protesters, an anti-establishment movement that faced off against President Emmanuel Macron’s Government in 2018-2019 over high fuel prices.

The violent outbursts were so intense that day that police lost control of ‌entire neighbourhoods to rioters and looters in France’s three largest cities: Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Every week since then, people have taken to the streets across France to voice their anger at police and the Government.

While the protests after October 17 were calmer, clashes erupted when police sought to disperse demonstrators as marches wound down. Officers repeatedly fired tear gas and charged groups of protesters who pelted them with bottles, paving stones and mortar-style fireworks. On October 24, far-right gangs entered the fray saying they wanted to protect businesses ‌and clashed with protesters in several cities, authorities said.

articles.title: How a bank collapse in Paraguay brought down the country’s President | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Following impeachment proceedings initiated against President Santiago Pena in connection with the collapse of a private lender holding savings for nearly half of the country’s population, Paraguay’s Senate voted to remove him for misconduct in office and placed him under house arrest on November 6. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as President.

The development comes just a day after Mr. Pena announced his resignation amid angry protests across the country over a financial crisis triggered by the collapse of a Ueno, a prominent digital lender-turned-bank that catered to nearly three million people and held about $800 million in public funds. Around 60% of the country’s adult population, abruptly, lost access to their savings accounts and pension payments after regulators took control of the bank, setting off a sequence of events that culminated in a change of political leadership.

articles.title: South Sudan postpones first national elections until February
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: South Sudan, the world’s newest country, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) postponed its first national elections from December to February amid growing ethnic and political battles.
The legislative and presidential elections had been scheduled for December 22, after already being delayed several times. The United Nations had warned that a vote could set off widespread conflict.
The electoral commission issued a new calendar on social media, giving a new voting date of February 11, with results to be announced four days later.
Commission secretary general Ahon Malou Lueth confirmed the change to AFP but would not give a reason or other details.
President Salva Kiir’s government forces and followers of detained former Vice President Riek Machar have been involved in escalating, deadly confrontations in recent months.
Other ethnic tensions and cattle-rustling battles have also complicated the picture in one of the world’s poorest countries.
South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011, but Mr. Kiir’s and Mr. Machar’s forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that killed at least 400,000 people.
Mr. Machar has been under house arrest since March 2025, accused of “crimes against humanity”.

The new election date was announced on the day that voter registration was due to start, with more than 3,100 centres set up across the country. Not all the necessary equipment had arrived at the centres, officials said.

The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan has issued several warnings about conditions in the country, including the displacement of tens of thousands of people, the deadly battles and the disruption of international humanitarian operations.
The commission has said that the tensions of recent months heighten “the risk of renewed conflict and atrocity crimes” while in October it said holding an election could spark renewed conflict.

articles.title: Avian influenza confirmed in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore; over 1,500 chickens culled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1) has been confirmed in chicken samples collected from a poultry farm at Kattiyankuppam village in Kurinjipadi taluk of Cuddalore district.

“The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, had confirmed the H5N1 avian influenza virus in samples collected from a poultry carcass on November 5, 2026,” District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar told The Hindu .

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre.

According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.”
He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.”

As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai.
On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said.
Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease.

“Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.
The carcasses are being disposed of through deep burial in designated pits, with bleaching powder applied and biosecurity measures in place.
An official said that movement of birds to and from the affected farms has been strictly restricted.

articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after hourslong global outage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.
Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.
The Redmond, Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.
It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

articles.title: Samsung announces Google co-developed smart glasses pricing and sale details
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Samsung has officially unveiled its new lineup of intelligent eyewear , bringing hands-free artificial intelligence into everyday fashion. Developed in partnership with Google, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the smart glasses integrate Google’s Gemini AI directly into stylish frames built for daily wear.

Set to launch on December 10, 2026, in the U.S. and South Korea, with pre-orders starting today, the collection features 30 distinct frame styles. Weighing around 41 grams, the frames combine Warby Parker’s classic look with Gentle Monster’s bold design aesthetics.

The smart glasses run on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform. Equipped with a 12 MP HD camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them. Wearers can ask Gemini to identify objects and landmarks, translate menus instantly or follow step-by-step navigation via Google Maps.

For workplace efficiency, the glasses can capture meeting whiteboards, generate key summaries and automatically sync them into Samsung Notes. The system also organises, summarises, and reads aloud incoming notifications.

To address privacy concerns, the eyewear design includes visible recording lights and audio chimes whenever the camera captures images or video. Additionally, the software claims to automatically blur bystanders’ faces during visual queries, while open-ear speakers are tuned to limit sound leakage.
The eyewear claims up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, extending up to 72 hours with its charging case.
The U.S. pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models, while Gentle Monster frames range from $449 to $489.

articles.title: Wider access to diabetes technology needs policy support, experts say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Diabetes management is moving beyond periodic finger-prick tests and clinic visits, with technologies such as continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), insulin pumps and mobile applications providing more detailed information on glucose levels and helping patients make day-to-day decisions about their care.

CGMs use a sensor placed on the arm or abdomen to measure glucose levels at regular intervals, offering a picture of fluctuations through the day and night. Insulin pumps deliver insulin continuously, while automated insulin delivery systems combine CGM readings with algorithms to adjust insulin delivery. Mobile applications can bring together information on glucose levels, food intake, physical activity and medication.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: IIT Roorkee student death: 70 exams postponed, to be held on November 22
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Following the death of a 20-year-old student, allegedly by suicide, at IIT Roorkee , the institute has postponed 70 examinations to November 22, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
The exams were originally scheduled to be held on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The deceased, Ayush Rajauria, was a second-year student of the institute’s BS-MS programme in Mathematics and Computing and hailed from Raj Nagar Extension in Ghaziabad.

According to police, the incident came to light around midnight on Thursday after Kuldeep Singh Negi, a security officer at IIT Roorkee, informed the Kotwali Roorkee police that a student was found dead in room number BS 10 on the second floor of Govind Bhawan hostel.
A purported note left by the deceased was found in his room, in which he allegedly wrote about suffering from depression and being distressed about his life, according to officials.
Officials said Rajauria had been receiving counselling on campus for the past year to cope with mental stress.

Speaking to PTI , Sonika Srivastava, in-charge of the IIT Roorkee's media cell, said the student was being counselled at the campus wellness centre — a facility dedicated to supporting students who may be experiencing depression or other psychological challenges.
She also said that all the students and their families have been informed about the postponement of the exams and the revised scheduled date, November 22.
Police said on Friday (November 13, 2026) that the student's family had been informed and an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death was underway.
In a statement, IIT Roorkee has expressed grief over the student's death and extended condolences to his family.

The death has sent shockwaves through students and parents, bringing the focus back on the mental health of IIT students across the country and the rising number of student suicides on campuses of the prestigious institutes.
(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050 and Speak2Us helpline at 9375493754.)

articles.title: Three phase gram panchayat polls in Bapatla district from November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Elections to 351 gram panchayats in Bapatla district will be conducted in three phases, with the first phase scheduled for November 26, District Collector V. Vinod Kumar announced on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
Addressing a media conference, he said elections would be held for 3,362 wards through 3,770 polling stations. The district has 8,67,954 voters, including 4,23,910 men, 4,43,995 women and 49 others.

The first phase will cover six mandals in the Parchur constituency, while the second will cover seven mandals in the Vemuru and Chirala constituencies. The third phase will cover seven mandals in the Bapatla and Repalle constituencies.

For the first phase, nominations will be accepted from November 15 to 17, followed by scrutiny on November 18. Appeals against rejected nominations can be filed on November 19 and will be resolved the next day. Candidates can withdraw nominations on November 21, when the final list will be published. Polling and counting will take place on November 26, followed by the election of deputy sarpanches.
Under G.O. No. 11, unanimous gram panchayat elections will attract development incentives of ₹15 lakh, ₹25 lakh and ₹50 lakh, depending on population.
The Collector also announced Bapatla municipality elections on November 26. He urged voters to verify their names in the electoral rolls and exercise their franchise.

articles.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Women must get adequate representation in Parliament, legislatures: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 14, 2026) stressed the need for adequate representation of women in Parliament and State legislatures, expressing hope that the Women’s Reservation Bill would be implemented soon. Incidentally, Karnataka is yet to have a woman representative in its Cabinet.

“The Women’s Reservation Bill has been passed in the Rajya Sabha and is yet to be approved by the Lok Sabha. I am hopeful that it will become a reality in the coming Parliament session. Women must get adequate representation in Parliament and State legislatures,” he said.
He was speaking after unveiling the logo of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region conference, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru on November 17 and 18.

Recalling former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s contribution to women’s political empowerment, Mr. Shivakumar said it was his government that had brought in legislation providing 50% reservation for women in local bodies, from panchayats to district-level administration. He said he believed that all political parties supported women’s reservation.

Highlighting women’s presence in important constitutional and administrative positions in Karnataka, he said the Governor, Chief Secretary, Karnataka Legislative Assembly Secretary, Legislative Council Secretary and Deputy Chairperson of the Legislative Council were all women.
“It is a matter of satisfaction that women are holding key positions in the State’s administration. Women are the eyes of a family. When women are empowered, men too become empowered,” he said.

Describing the CWP conference as a historic milestone for Karnataka, Mr. Shivakumar said the State government would extend all support to the first independent CWP India Region conference being held in Bengaluru.

The conference, being organised under the leadership of CWP India Region president D. Purandeswari, is expected to bring together more than 150 women parliamentarians, legislators and presiding officers from India and abroad.
The participants are expected to deliberate on the country’s development and protection of women’s rights, he said.

The government would extend all necessary assistance through Legislative Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed to ensure the successful conduct of the conference, he said.

Mr. Shivakumar also recalled the contributions of former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Sucheta Kripalani, the country’s first woman Chief Minister, and President Droupadi Murmu.
Their achievements demonstrated that women could accomplish anything they set their minds to, he added.

Another 2.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Doda at 1:09 p.m., at a depth of 10 km.
A 3.9-magnitude earthquake was recorded in Leh, Ladakh, at 10:29 a.m., at a depth of 10 km.

articles.title: Cyclone may bring isolated heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh from November 18 to 20
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Amaravati, has given a heavy rain forecast for the coastal A.P. from November 18 to 20, though no such warnings have been given on November 16 and 17, when the cyclonic storm is likely to make a landfall.

According to the IMD’s afternoon bulletin, heavy rain is likely at one or two places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and gusty winds, with speed reaching 40-50 kmph, on November 18, 19 and 20. The State may not see much rain during the landfall.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the low-pressure over southeast Bay of Bengal strengthened into a well-marked low pressure. It is very likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression over the same region by Sunday (November 15, 2026). Thereafter, it is likely to move north-northwestwards and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal around November 16.

Weather experts at the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority and IMD have said clarity on the probable landfall location may emerge after depression is formed. At present, weather models are showing varied results, they said.

However, the IMD has said that squally weather, with wind speeds gusting up to 60 kmph, is very likely to prevail near the Southeast Bay of Bengal on November 14 and 15. It may increase further to 70 kmph on November 16 and 17. Near the Southwest Bay of Bengal, the wind speed may touch 80 kmph on November 17, and near the central parts, the gales may touch 75-85 kmph speed from November 17.
The sea condition is likely to be rough to very rough over southeast, southwest and central parts of the Bay from November 15.
Fishermen have been advised to return to coasts by November 15.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.
Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July.
“India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.

fullParagraphs: The bitumen carrier, Atlantic Asphalt, that rammed into riverboat American Heritage in New Orleans does not have Indian crew onboard.
